nieuw.titel: Use impassable terrain to create safe lanes for advancing
nieuw.tekst: Use impassable terrain to create a lane where a unit can attack, advance after winning combat and escape an enemy charge on the following turn.
nieuw.waarom: He values being able to keep moving forward after winning a combat while the terrain protects the unit from a counterattack.
nieuw.voorbeeld: His Mortis Engine fitted into a narrow pocket beside the Herdstone, where he found its unusual base size a major advantage.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He was unsure whether any other base size could have fitted into that pocket.

bronnen.citaat: you can create a lane for your unit to surge forward and then escape

nieuw.titel: Use impassable terrain to restrict enemy frontage
nieuw.tekst: Try to hem advancing enemy units in against impassable terrain and limit the frontage they can use.
nieuw.waarom: He says restricting frontage makes it awkward for the enemy to move and limits their options.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He consciously tried to limit the frontage of the opposing Dragon Ogres as they advanced across the board.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He warns that terrain used to block line of sight or maintain control of a position can also hem in your own units.

extraCitaten.citaat: ham your opponent in and limit their options.

nieuw.titel: Attack skirmishers where terrain obstructs forming ranks
nieuw.tekst: Look for a charge into one side of a large skirmishing unit where impassable terrain prevents models from reaching the rear ranks when forming up. He recommends exploiting this vulnerability to remove skirmishers.
nieuw.waarom: He identifies coherency as a weakness of large skirmishing units. In his game, moving around the impassable terrain used more distance than some models could cover when forming ranks.
nieuw.voorbeeld: His Mortis Engine charged beside the Herdstone, and about half the opposing skirmishing unit died because it could not form up around the terrain.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: His event's judge required the models to form ranks and fit through the gap rather than scatter around the terrain; that ruling determined which models could reach their positions.

bronnen.citaat: if you can hit them on one side

extraCitaten.citaat: they have to go around this impossible terrain and that's measurable distance

nieuw.titel: Use impassable terrain to shorten enemy retreats
nieuw.tekst: Try to force enemies to flee towards impassable terrain so they cannot escape as far and are easier to catch. He suggests terrain-creating spells can make this easier to arrange.
nieuw.waarom: He argues that even if the fleeing unit is allowed to snake around the obstacle, moving sideways costs movement rather than increasing its distance from pursuers.
nieuw.voorbeeld: His opponent's Black Orc Mob had to flee towards impassable terrain. The judge ruled that it could not pivot to move away, and his Grave Guard caught it in pursuit.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He acknowledges that other players may disagree with the ruling that the fleeing unit could not move at all.

bronnen.citaat: reduce their ability to flee around those types

extraCitaten.citaat: it's going to cost him movement to move sideways.

bron.citaat: that crystal column blocked all line of sight

extraCitaten.citaat: to put it in that gap to give me another turn of battle points.

aanvullingen.voorbeeld: He tried to bridge a gap between terrain pieces with Crystal Column to block the magic-missile firing lane to his Terrorgheist, but his opponent dispelled it. In another game, he wanted Crystal Column in a gap to delay a charge and gain another turn of objective points.
aanvullingen.toelichting: Using Crystal Column to obstruct firing and charging lanes is the same recommendation as using control spells to block those lanes.

overgeslagen: Skipped sponsorship, channel and tournament news, results, general rules commentary and garbled unit or character names. Kept the event-specific rulings qualified rather than presenting them as universal rules.
